summary:
Earth Terminal is a Bloomberg Terminal inspired interface for planetary forensics built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Earth System Trend Detective challenge. Designed for students, educators, and citizen scientists, it takes 24 years (2002–2025) of monthly NASA and NOAA Earth observations, across air temperature, precipitation, root-zone soil moisture, sea surface temperature, ocean chlorophyll-a, and surface solar radiation, into an interactive 3D globe and statistical suite.
Users filter global trends in real time using a continuous p-value significance slider that flattens random climate noise while highlighting statistically verified hotspots. Selecting any region reveals seasonally seperated anomaly time series, Theil–Sen slopes, Mann–Kendall significance tests, Student’s t-tests, and 95% confidence intervals. Users can overlay secondary variables with lead/lag cross-correlation, discover opposing global teleconnection dipoles linked by 3D globe arcs, hear data rates via spatial Web Audio sonar, and generate hypotheses from a grounded AI Climatologist
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Earth Terminal is an interactive 3D Earth-observation workstation modelled on financial trading terminals. It tracks 24 years (2002–2025) of monthly NASA and NOAA satellite data across six variables: 2-metre air temperature (MERRA2:T2M), precipitation (GPM:PRECIP), soil moisture (GLDAS:SOIL), sea surface temperature (JPL:SST), ocean chlorophyll-a (MODIS:CHLA), and surface solar radiation (CERES:SW). On the 3D globe, column height shows the rate of change and colour shows direction (cyan for increases, crimson for decreases). Dragging the live p-value slider flattens random climate noise in real time, leaving only statistically significant trends standing.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Clicking any region opens a 24-year time-series chart and statistical tear-sheet. Users can remove seasonal cycles, brush custom date windows, overlay secondary variables, and run Mann–Kendall tests, Theil–Sen slopes, Student’s t-tests, and 95% confidence intervals. A one-click Dipole Finder links oppositely trending regions with 3D globe arcs, while a guided Detective Mode, interactive 8-step tutorial, hover tooltips, and grounded AI Climatologist make rigorous climate analysis approachable for students, educators, and citizen scientists.


Tools, Creativity & Design Considerations
Built with Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Jotai, Recharts, and react-globe.gl (Three.js/WebGL), backed by a pure TypeScript statistical engine verified against Python scipy.stats. To balance speed with live data access, we pre-baked 10°×10° global grids for smooth 60 FPS rendering while querying live NASA POWER and NOAA ERDDAP APIs with automatic offline fallback. We also built a procedural Web Audio sonar synthesiser that lets users hear trend speeds and statistical significance as they sweep across the globe.
